posts.text:
if your closet is organized by color, you are either a genius or hiding a very chaotic inner life. 

be honest.
women who thrift purely for the hunt and never actually wear what they find are just collectors, not stylists.
the weirdest realization is when you finally find your ‘uniform’ and realize you’re never going to wear half the trends you obsessed over.
the best outfit you’ve ever worn was definitely a total accident involving clothes you were too tired to put away.
wearing a coat when it’s 60 degrees out: a high-fashion necessity or just someone who can't handle a breeze?
if you actually wear everything in your closet, you’re either lying or you’re a minimalist who needs more chaos.
taking your shoes off at someone’s house and realizing your socks don’t match your vibe is a specific kind of internal panic.
people who keep the tags on their clothes until they leave the house are living life on the edge.
the micro-trend cycle is just a elaborate way to keep you buying things that will look ridiculous by june.
if your 'going out' shoes aren't broken in, you aren't going out, you're just volunteering for a foot injury.
oversized everything is either the height of luxury or you just gave up on your tailor.

some of us genuinely enjoy the physical act of getting ready. 

the rest of you are just guessing.
nothing ruins a good outfit faster than realizing you have to carry a jacket all night because it doesn't match.

tell me your stance on denim on denim. 

it’s either a total power move or you’re headed to a tractor pull.
the only people who actually believe 'it’s just fashion' are the ones who don't have a signature look.

people who wear all black in the middle of summer are just superior. 

change my mind.
nothing humbles you faster than buying a piece you loved online only for it to look like a costume the second it arrives.
the audacity of a dress that doesn’t have pockets is honestly the reason i have trust issues.
people who own multiples of the exact same shirt in different colors: are you okay, or have you just solved the matrix?
half the people saying they want a 'capsule wardrobe' just want permission to never have to make a decision again.
getting a stain on a brand new white shirt within five minutes of wearing it is a canon event for some of us.

wearing a bra that matches your outfit feels like a tiny secret superpower.

or are we all just team comfort at this point?
the 'it looks better on the hanger' trap is the only reason i have a pile of clothes i’ve never worn.
everyone claims they dress for comfort until they find that one piece that makes them feel untouchable. then comfort goes out the window.

the thrift store hunt is a personality trait. 

you either love the dirt or you hate the process.
there are two types of people: those who know exactly what they’re wearing tomorrow, and those who are currently panicking.
if you have to adjust your top every thirty seconds, it isn't an outfit, it's a part-time job.
wearing pajamas outside because you’re ‘ironic’ is fine, but let’s be honest: we just didn't want to change.

you’re either a ‘one bag for the whole week’ person or you’re lying to yourself.

pick your side.
people who say they dress for comfort are usually the ones hiding their best outfits for an audience.
those who iron their clothes before heading to the grocery store: are you healing, or just bored?
the post-laundry realization that you have nothing to wear is a special kind of betrayal.
realizing your 'signature style' is just a rotation of the same three silhouettes.

stiletto people vs flat shoe people. 

there is a fundamental lifestyle difference here that no one talks about.
owning clothes that still have the tags on is just an expensive way of saying you haven't figured out your identity yet.

if you think you can hide behind an oversized blazer, you’re wrong. 

you’re actually just highlighting the fact that you’re hiding.

the most judgmental people at brunch aren't the ones in designer gear. 

it’s the ones in a plain white tee that fits perfectly.

the 2-minute morning panic of realizing your coat ruins the entire outfit. 

we’ve all been there.
you’re either a ‘dress up for the airport’ person or you belong in the cargo hold with the suitcases.

the ‘effortless’ messy bun look actually takes more effort than a sleek blowout.

we need to stop lying to ourselves.
if you keep an outfit in your closet for a ‘special occasion’ that never comes, you’re just curating a museum for your own indecision.
nothing humbles you faster than realizing the outfit you planned in your head looks like a cry for help in the mirror.

women who can wear white after labor day without spilling coffee are not human.

what is your secret.
everyone claims they have a ‘uniform’ but most of you are just wearing the same mistake in four different colors.

stop pretending you like 'eclectic' layers. 

you just haven't found a single top that covers what you need it to cover yet.

belt with loops or tucking the excess into the waistband.

there is a right answer and it says everything about your personality.
women who can wear head-to-toe black and make it look like a choice instead of a depression nap: how.

the audacity of a zipper failing while you're already ten minutes late. 

some fabrics clearly have a personal vendetta against us.
you don't actually like vintage shopping. you like the idea of finding something cool so you can tell people where you got it.

there are two types of people:

1. those who store clothes by color.
2. those who store them by ‘vibes’.

which one is the actual chaotic evil?
people who re-wear their ‘going out’ tops to the office are the bravest people i know.
owning more than three pairs of the exact same trousers isn't ‘finding your fit.’ it’s just a lack of imagination.
wearing your most uncomfortable, expensive heels to a grocery store is a power move.
the ‘capsule wardrobe’ trend is just a way for people to feel superior about having less stuff.
there is a special level of hell for people who wear outdoor shoes inside their own home.
you’re either someone who keeps their receipts in case of buyer’s remorse, or you burn them immediately to forget the damage.
trying to find a skirt that sits on your actual waist without sliding down to your hips is an extreme sport.
if you can’t sit down comfortably in your outfit, you aren’t dressed; you’re just in a costume.

you’re either someone who wears a coat over their shoulders like a cape or you use the sleeves like a normal person.

there is no middle ground.

people who iron their pajamas. 

i just want to know if you're actually okay.

the people who actually enjoy folding laundry aren’t human. 

what kind of psychiatric help do you need?
we need to talk about the physical pain of finding out your favorite pair of pants is now too small because of the dryer.
that one friend who buys a dress for a specific event and never wears it again is keeping the economy alive.

dry clean only: 

1. a necessary maintenance task 
2. a reason to never wear the item again 

which one are you?
if your pockets can’t hold your phone, it’s not an outfit. it’s a decorative fabric display.

the ‘i’m just running errands’ outfit that actually took forty minutes to assemble. 

we see you.

everyone claims to love thrifting until they find a stain on a shirt from 1994. 

then the ‘vintage charm’ disappears pretty fast.
the girls who keep the original tags on until they leave the house are living in a permanent state of anxiety.
everyone who insists they look better in natural lighting is just scared of a ring light because they can't hide their flaws.
people who claim they don't care about trends but replace their entire wardrobe every six months are the real scammers.
you’re either someone who checks the weather three times before picking an outfit, or you’re the person shivering in a crop top because it looked good in the mirror.
stop pretending you like 'breathable' fabrics. you just like clothes that don't make you sweat through your day.
the audacity of a zipper that gets stuck halfway up your back is a personal attack from the manufacturer.
buying an outfit specifically for a photo and then never wearing it again is a cry for help.
you either identify as a maximalist in the morning or you’re lying to yourself about your personality.
the most judgmental people at the office are always the ones wearing the most uncomfortable shoes.
if you don’t have a ‘bad day’ sweater that you refuse to wash for three days straight, are you even doing it right?
layering more than two pieces is just an elaborate way to avoid doing laundry for another week.
you’re either someone who wears your jewelry in the shower or you aren’t allowed to handle nice things.
if you think heels are the only way to look put-together for dinner, you’re just not trying hard enough with your flats.
buying things in neutrals isn't a personality. it’s just a fear of being perceived.
everyone who says they 'don't care about fashion' is currently wearing the exact clothes someone else told them to buy.
there is no greater betrayal than a pair of shoes that look incredible but refuse to let you walk more than three blocks.
you’re either a ‘dress up for the grocery store’ person or you’ve given up on society entirely. pick one.
stop calling it a ‘capsule wardrobe.’ you just haven’t found anything you actually like wearing yet.

if you store your clothes by color, you’re organized. 

if you store them by ‘vibe,’ you’re dangerous.
the most expensive items in my closet are always the ones i’m too terrified to actually wear out.
people who iron their underwear might be the only ones truly winning at life right now.

thrift store hunters or luxury mall shoppers. 

one of you is obsessed with the chase, and the other just likes the receipt.
folding your clothes into neat little squares is just a hobby for people who don’t have enough to do.

everyone acting like they don't look in the mirror every time they pass a window. 

stop it. we see you.
the best outfits are always constructed at 2am when you have absolutely nowhere to be the next day.

wearing a full monochromatic look isn't a fashion statement. 

it’s just proof you don’t have the energy to match patterns before noon.
you’re either someone who checks the fabric content label immediately or you’re the reason fast fashion exists.
people who wear pajamas to the coffee shop: are you feeling peaceful or did you lose the will to participate in society today?
nothing reveals a person’s true priorities faster than whether they hang their clothes or leave them on a chair.
the ‘i’ll wear this when i lose weight’ box is just a graveyard for perfectly good outfits.
owning more than five pairs of jeans but wearing the same one every week is a lifestyle.
the weirdest part of getting dressed is realizing you’re actually just dressing as a version of yourself you hope people believe exists.
if you keep the tags on until you actually leave the house, we need to talk about your trust issues.
